sanskrit: udyann ādityo ghuṇān hantu sūryo nimrocan raśmibhir hantu | tāvan no abhisaṃhitam ||
english: Rising, may Āditya slay the woodworms; setting, may Sūrya slay them with his rays. So long has he been marshalled against us.

sanskrit: apsarā mūlam akhanad gandharvaḥ pary abravīt | tena vo vṛtrahā sūryo ni jambhyām̐ amṛtad ghuṇāḥ ||
english: The Apsarā dug out the root; the Gandharva recited it round about. By that very means may Sūrya, slayer of Vṛtra, crush you woodworms and strip you of immortality.

sanskrit: ghuṇān hantv āyatī ghuṇān hantu parāyatī | ghuṇān avaghnatī hantu ghuṇān pinaṣṭu piṃṣatī ||
english: Let her coming slay the woodworms; let her going slay the woodworms. Let her striking slay the woodworms; let her who grinds grind the woodworms to dust.

sanskrit: ghuṇā na kiṃ caneha vaḥ pratibuddhā abhūtana | pradoṣaṃ taskarā iva ||
english: Woodworms, let there be nothing of yours here; you have been detected, like thieves caught at nightfall.

sanskrit: ghuṇānāṃ madhyato jyeṣṭhaḥ kaniṣṭha uta madhyamaḥ | hatā vaḥ sarve jñātayo hatā mātā hataḥ pitā ||
english: Among the woodworms, the eldest, and likewise the youngest and the middle one — slain are all your kindred, slain is the mother, slain is the father.

sanskrit: yathā phena udakena dadṛśāno nijasyati | evā vayaṃ ghuṇān sarvān sākaṃ vācā ni jāsayāmasi ||
english: Just as foam, seen upon the water, is swept away, so we with one utterance drive out all the woodworms together.

sanskrit: ni gāvo goṣṭhe asadan ni mṛgāso avikṣata | ni tvam āditya raśmibhir ghuṇān sarvām̐ ajījasaḥ ||
english: The cows have settled in the stall; the wild beasts have retreated. You, O Āditya, with your rays have driven all the woodworms down.

sanskrit: udyan raśmīn ā tanuṣva bāṇavadbhiḥ sam arpaya | ghuṇāṃs tvaṃ sarvān āditya ghorayā tanvā tapa ||
english: Rising, stretch forth your rays; dispatch them like arrows. You, O Āditya, scorch all the woodworms with your terrible body.

sanskrit: ya ānataḥ parāṇato dāror ivāpatakṣaṇam | śarkoṭo nāma vā asi kutas tvaṃ viṣavān asaḥ ||
english: You who are curved and bent back, chipping away like a piece of wood — Śarkoṭa is indeed your name. Whence have you come to possess venom?

sanskrit: ya ubhayena praharasi pucchena cāsyena ca | āsye cana te viṣaṃ kutas te pucchadhāv asat ||
english: You who strike with both — with your tail and with your mouth — even in your mouth there is no venom; whence should venom reside in the track of your tail?

sanskrit: vidutsurasya dānavasya tasya tvaṃ napād asi | tasyāgre 'rasaṃ viṣaṃ tatas tavārasaṃ viṣam ||
english: You are the grandson of the Dānava Vidutsura. His venom was rendered powerless at the start; therefore your venom too is powerless.

sanskrit: arasārasaṃ tvākaraṃ vadhre vadhriṃ tvākaram | vadhriṃ tvā cakrur devā amṛtāsa āsuram ||
english: I have made you utterly powerless, impotent — a castrate I have made you. The immortal gods made you, the demonic one, a castrate.

sanskrit: iyattakaḥ kuṣumbhakas takaṃ bhinadmi śamyayā | tato viṣaṃ parāsicam apācīm anu saṃvatam ||
english: Such a tiny, little creature — I split that creature with a peg. Thereupon I poured away the venom in the southern direction along the year.

sanskrit: imāḥ paścā mayūryaḥ sapta svasāro agruvaḥ | tās te viṣaṃ vi jahrira udakaṃ kumbhinīr iva kūpāt kulijinīr iva ||
english: These seven peahens to the west, sisters, unmarried virgins — they drew out your venom, as water-bearers draw water from a well, as those who own pitchers draw it.

sanskrit: navānāṃ navatīnām ity eka ||
english: "Of the nine nineties" — thus the one verse.

sanskrit: vrātam aham apakṣṇānāṃ vrātaṃ muṇḍīyasām uta | vrātaṃ muṇḍivlānām ahaṃ pra dhvāṅkṣām̐ iva cātaye ||
english: I drive away the troop of the wing-clipped ones, the troop of the baldheads, and also the troop of the shaven-headed ones, even as crows are chased away.

sanskrit: pravaktā pramādayitā nidrā tandrīs tṛtīyakaḥ | tāñ jaṅgiḍasyāgninā sarvān prati dahāmasi||
english: The prattler, the infatuator, Drowsiness, Languor, and Fever-of-the-third-day — all of them we burn up with the fire of the jaṅgiḍa plant.

sanskrit: aśuddhān naḥ pari pāhi rakṣobhya uta jaṅgiḍa | yātudhānāt kimīdinas tasmān naḥ pāhi jaṅgiḍa ||
english: Protect us, O Jaṅgiḍa, from the unclean ones, and from the Rakṣases. From the Yātudhāna and the Kimīdin — from these protect us, O Jaṅgiḍa.

sanskrit: apsarābhyo gandharvebhyo devebhyo asurebhyaḥ | atho sarvasmāt pāpmanas tasmān naḥ pāhi jaṅgiḍa ||
english: From Apsarases, from Gandharvas, from gods, from Asuras, and moreover from all evil — from these protect us, O Jaṅgiḍa.

sanskrit: ni te śatrūn dahati devo agnir nir arātim amatiṃ yātudhānān | ā yāhi śatrūn duritāpaghnañ chatān no yakṣmebhyaḥ pari pāhi jaṅgiḍa ||
english: The divine Agni burns down your enemies, drives away hostility, folly, and the Yātudhānas. Come forth, destroyer of enemies and misfortune; protect us, O Jaṅgiḍa, from a hundred diseases.

sanskrit: akarmāgnim adhipām asya devam anvārapsva sahasā daivyena | sahasvān naḥ sahasā pātu jaṅgiḍo yathā jayema pṛtanājyeṣu ||
english: Attach yourself to the divine Agni, its overlord, with divine power — the one who does the work. May the powerful Jaṅgiḍa guard us with power, so that we may be victorious in battles.

sanskrit: satyo agniḥ satyā āpaḥ satye me dyāvāpṛthivī viśvaśaṃbhuvau | satyam idaṃ brahmāsmākaṃ kṛtam astu yam abadhnād uśanendrāya taṃ te badhnāmi jaṅgiḍam ||
english: True is Agni, true are the Waters, true to me are Heaven and Earth, the two that bring welfare to all. True shall be this sacred formula of ours that is made. The jaṅgiḍa that Uśanas bound for Indra — that same I bind upon you.
